title: Observation of Non-linear hall effect in Polycrystalline magnetic multilayes
authors: Preet Kamal, Chirag kalouni, Amiya Mondal, Awadesh Narayan, Debangsu Roy
abstract: The Nonlinear Hall effect(NLHE) driven principally by the Berry curvature dipole has been established in non-centrosymmetric vander Waals crystals, topological semimetals, and moiré superlattices, but its extension to technologically mature heavy-metal/ferromagnet multilayer platforms remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the observation of a robust NLHE in polycrystalline magnetic multilayers, persisting from 2 K to room temperature. The second-harmonic transverse voltage is independent of both excitation frequency and applied out-of-plane magnetic field, while the vanishingly small third-harmonic response confirms that the observed signal is not dominated by a quantum-metric contribution and instead reflects a genuine second-order electronic response. A scaling analysis of the second-order Hall conductivity against the longitudinal conductivity identifies a dominant, conductivity-independent term establishing the intrinsic berry curvature dipole. Our theoretical analysis, supported by first-principles DFT calculations, further satisfies and corroborates the experimental results. These results establish sputter-deposited polycrystalline thin film as the first engineered magnetic multilayer platform for BCD-driven nonlinear Hall transport, extending the NLHE material landscape beyond van der Waals systems into scalable, industry-compatible thin-film spintronic architectures suitable for high frequency rectifications and nonlinear sensors.
summary: This work reports the observation of a robust Nonlinear Hall Effect (NLHE) in polycrystalline magnetic multilayers. By measuring second-harmonic voltages and performing theoretical calculations, the authors prove that this effect originates from the intrinsic Berry curvature dipole generated at interfaces. This establishes these scalable thin films as a promising new platform for next-generation nonlinear spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to observe and characterize the Nonlinear Hall Effect (NLHE) in technologically relevant magnetic multilayer platforms, extending its understanding beyond van der Waals crystals.
main_result: A robust NLHE was observed in polycrystalline magnetic multilayers, confirming that the effect is driven by the intrinsic Berry curvature dipole (BCD), establishing these films as a new platform for spintronic applications.
method: The research combines transport measurements of second-harmonic transverse voltage ($V_{xy}^{2\omega}$) with theoretical analysis using first-principles DFT calculations to confirm the underlying electronic mechanism.
model_or_system: The system is a polycrystalline magnetic multilayer heterostructure, specifically $	ext{Ta}/	ext{Pt}/[	ext{Ir}/	ext{Fe}/	ext{Co}/	ext{Pt}]_5/	ext{Pt}$. The physics is governed by spin-orbit coupling and broken structural inversion symmetry at the interfaces.
key_observables: Second-harmonic transverse voltage ($V_{xy}^{2\omega}$), which shows quadratic dependence on current, frequency independence, and magnetic field independence; also measured $R_{xx}$, $V_{xy}^{1\omega}$, and XRD patterns.
important_parameters: Temperature range (2 K to room temperature); applied magnetic fields ($\pm 2 	ext{ T}$); multilayer periodicity ($[\dots]_5$).
main_assumptions: The observed NLHE signal is assumed to be dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature dipole mechanism, supported by vanishing third-harmonic response and scaling analysis.
figures_summary: Figures show layer architecture, Hall bar geometry, $R_{xx}$ vs. T (metallic behavior), XRD patterns confirming texture, linear transport measurements ($V^{1\omega}$), and nonlinear measurements ($V^{2\omega}$) showing quadratic dependence on current.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the measurement setup by measuring linear transport; it then measures the second-harmonic voltage to confirm a genuine nonlinear response; finally, theoretical analysis (DFT) links this observed signal magnitude directly to the intrinsic Berry curvature dipole component ($D_{yz}$).
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics, the reliance on quantum geometric effects like the BCD and symmetry analysis mirrors concepts used in topological materials research relevant to AMO physics.
